ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, and authorized signatories against the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit domestic watchlist, UN Security Council consolidated lists, US OFAC SDN list, EU consolidated financial sanctions list, and Samoa Police/justice sector records; PEPs require enhanced due diligence, a written source-of-funds explanation, beneficial-ownership corroboration, and senior management approval at the licensed registered agent, consistent with the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2018 and SIFA guidance.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) — International Companies and Trust Registry; name clearance is effected exclusively through SIFA-licensed registered agents (no direct public self-service portal)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be expressed in English or in Roman/Latin characters; names in the Samoan language (Gagana Samoa) are permitted using the standard Samoan alphabet; suffixes such as 'Limited' are optional for Samoan international companies; a name must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name and must comply with the International Companies Act 1987 s. 9 and the Companies Act 2001 s. 20 prohibitions.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Government / Crown / State Patronage terms implying connection with the Government of Samoa
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the SIFA-licensed registered agent files a written administrative appeal with the SIFA Registrar within 14 days of the rejection notice, restating the proposed name with an availability re-check; the Registrar issues a final written administrative determination; a further refusal may be challenged by an application for judicial review to the Supreme Court of Samoa under the Judicature Act 1961 within 28 days, supported by affidavit; an extension of a pending name reservation must be requested before expiry using SIFA's prescribed extension application and fee.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is not a substitute for the statutory registered office: the International Companies Act 1987 requires a physical registered office in Samoa maintained at the licensed registered agent's address; however, the commercial operations of this AIGC video-SaaS entity may be conducted wholly remotely, and the tax-exempt international company model permits minimal physical presence in Samoa provided annual agent fees, statutory filings, and registered-agent obligations are maintained.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low — estimated annual probability below 5% over the first three years for a low AML/CFT-risk software entity absent PEP involvement, sanctioned-jurisdiction exposure, or compliance red flags; SIFA and the Samoa FIU generally target inspections at higher-risk licensees and non-compliant registered agents.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 2023 (Samoa), ss. 5-8 (Formation), s. 9 (Certificate of Incorporation), s. 10 (Effects of Incorporation), ss. 15-16 (Registered Office and Registered Agent); Business Licences Act 2002 (Samoa) for domestic operating licence; relevant fees under International Companies (Fees) Regulations
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA), acting in coordination with the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL) Companies Registry, Apia, Samoa
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Certificate of Incorporation issued under section 9 of the International Companies Act 2023, together with registered Memorandum of Association and Articles of Association
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is prescribed under the International Companies Act 2023; an International Company may issue one or more shares of no par value, commonly subscribed with a nominal total of US$1.00. No escrow account, capital deposit, or paid-up capital certification is required as a precondition to incorporation for a non-resident-owned private International Company.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, by the sole initial director of [Company Name] Limited, that: (1) The share subscriptions tendered by the initial subscribers are approved and the ordinary shares set out in the Register of Members are hereby allotted and issued as fully paid or paid-up to such amount as the directors determine. (2) The registered office located in Apia, Samoa, and the licensed registered agent appointed therefor are adopted as the statutory registered office and agent of the Company. (3) The appointments of the director(s) and officers named in the Register of Directors and Officers are ratified and approved. (4) The affixing of the company seal, execution of bank documents, submission of incorporation filings, and all administrative acts necessary to give effect to these resolutions are hereby authorized.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA), lodged via a SIFA-licensed International Company Service Provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit to SIFA a written name clearance and reservation request, either directly or through the licensed agent portal, proposing the intended company name together with customer due diligence (CDD) particulars of the subscribers. The Registrar verifies that the name is not identical or misleadingly similar to an existing registered name and contains no restricted word (such as Bank, Trust, Insurance, or Reinsurance) without regulatory consent. The approved name is reserved for a limited statutory period pending formal incorporation.
required_dossiers: Name availability/reservation application form
Anti-money-laundering CDD pack for all beneficial owners and subscribers
Proposed corporate name with lawful designator suffix (Limited, Ltd, Incorporated, or Inc.)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or queried, file a revised name application immediately; alternatively submit a written appeal for reconsideration to the Registrar within 14 days of refusal, supported by explanatory submissions distinguishing the proposed name from conflicting registrations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed International Company Service Provider in Samoa, with notarial attestation before a Samoan Notary Public
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Memorandum of Association and Articles of Association in conformity with the International Companies Act 2023, including no-par-value share authority, single-director governance, distributions policy, and restricted-object wording. Each subscriber executes the memorandum before a witness and signatures are notarized. The registered office and registered agent are expressly identified in the constitution and their written consents attached.
required_dossiers: Memorandum of Association (executed and dated)
Articles of Association (executed and dated)
Witness attestation and notarial certificates
Consent of proposed registered agent to act
Certificate of subscriber identity and signature verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar rejects any constitutional provision as noncompliant, amend the offending clause, re-execute the memorandum and articles before the same or substitute notary, and resubmit with a corrective cover letter addressing the noted defects.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of the Incorporation Application with the Registrar
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA), registration window at Apia
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the incorporation application form, the executed and notarized constitution, consent of the registered agent, declarations or consents of the initial directors and officers, confirmation of registered office address, and evidenced payment of the statutory incorporation duty. The Registrar examines compliance with the International Companies Act 2023, assigns the registration number, and registers the company upon full satisfaction.
required_dossiers: Incorporation application form for an International Company
Executed Memorandum of Association and Articles of Association
Consent of Registered Agent to act
Declaration and consent of initial director(s) and officer(s)
Registered office confirmation in Samoa
Receipt of government filing fee payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a requisition or enquiry, respond within the prescribed statutory period with amended documents or supplemental particulars; where registration is refused, cure the stated defect and re-file, or apply for administrative reconsideration in writing with supporting legal submissions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and Certified Constitution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon due registration, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation stating the company name, registration number, date of incorporation, and liability type, together with a certified copy of the registered constitution. The company becomes a body corporate with perpetual succession and the capacity of a natural person, effective as of the certificate date.
required_dossiers: Approved registration file with constitutional documents
Official registry fee receipt
Registered agent acknowledgment of certified copy custody
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Certificate of Incorporation contains clerical errors in company name, number, or effective date, request a corrected certificate under the Registrar's rectification power; substantive changes must be effected through Articles of Amendment and a fresh registry filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Governance, First Board Resolution, and Statutory Register Establishment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company's initial director and/or board of directors, acting with the SIFA-licensed registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Adopt the pro-forma first board resolution in writing or at a duly convened board meeting; approve the share subscription and allotment, adopt the Samoan registered office and registered agent, and ratify the appointment of directors and officers. Establish the Register of Members, Register of Directors and Officers, Register of Charges, and issue share certificates; deliver required particulars to the registered agent and maintain the company seal in accordance with the International Companies Act 2023.
required_dossiers: Written first board resolution or board minutes
Share subscription and allotment records
Register of Members
Register of Directors and Officers
Share certificates issued to subscribers
Consents and declarations of officers
Certified certificates of incorporation and constitution
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registered agent or a compliance review queries any governance document, cure incomplete registers, re-execute defective consents, and file supplementary declarations; resubmission in corrected form is accepted until full statutory compliance with the Act is achieved.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Business Licensing Division, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Samoa
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Business Licence issued under the Business Licences Act 2002 (Samoa) for the conduct of AI software development, SaaS platform operation, and digital content generation from a Samoan registered office or premises

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE) acting through the Planning and Urban Management Agency (PUMA), Samoa
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Screening and Registration category for office-based ICT and software development activities; a full Environmental Impact Assessment Report is not required in the absence of manufacturing, chemical processing, or large-scale physical infrastructure
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Office-only operations: zero industrial wastewater discharge; no point-source VOC or stack emission thresholds apply to software operations; general solid waste and e-waste handling must comply with the Waste Management Act 2005 and all discarded IT equipment must be disposed of through licensed recyclers or approved collection channels

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety clearance and certification from the Samoa Fire and Emergency Services Authority (SFESA) covering the leased Apia office premises; structural load and occupancy inspection for the office floor area; occupational health and safety clearance issued by the Occupational Safety and Health Division of MCIL under the Labour and Employment Relations Act 2013, including emergency evacuation protocols and first-aid compliance for the workforce

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry of Revenue (MOR), Independent State of Samoa — official tax administration portal: www.revenue.gov.ws; administered under the Tax Administration Act 2012, Income Tax Act 2012, and Goods and Services Tax Act 2003
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: An International Company (IC) incorporated under the International Companies Act 1987 is automatically exempt from all Samoan national taxes, including income tax and VAGST, under section 193 of that Act. No TIN or VAGST registration number is required for the IC's offshore business operations (e.g., AI Avatar Video Generation SaaS). The IC obtains only its Certificate of Incorporation from the Registrar of Companies within the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL) and pays an annual government fee. If the IC voluntarily supplies taxable domestic goods or services in Samoa, or sustains WST 200,000 or more in annual taxable turnover sourced from Samoa, it must apply to the MOR for VAGST registration on Form VAGST-1, accompanied by certified constitutional documents, director identification, and a non-resident ownership declaration where applicable.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election exists under Samoan law. The tax exemption for International Companies is automatic and mandatory under section 193 of the International Companies Act 1987, and disqualification occurs only if the IC conducts business with Samoan residents in breach of that section. No hybrid mismatch election or limitation-on-benefits election is available; Samoa has no BEPS Action 2 hybrid legislation applicable to ICs, and only the general anti-avoidance rule in the Tax Administration Act 2012 may operate in cases of artificial arrangements.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAGST (Value Added Goods and Services Tax)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: WST 200,000 annual taxable turnover (mandatory); voluntary registration permitted for lower-turnover suppliers of taxable goods or services
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time e-invoicing, API-based fiscal clearance, or digital stamping regime is currently in force in Samoa. The Commissioner of Revenue may prescribe electronic filing and record-keeping methods through the MOR's EFile portal, but invoices issued by VAGST-registered suppliers remain standard tax invoices in arrears containing prescribed particulars. Records must be retained for 5 years. Digital SaaS services exported to non-residents fall outside any domestic invoicing mandate and are zero-rated or exempt.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating at 0% applies to exported goods and to services supplied solely to a non-resident recipient for use or benefit wholly outside Samoa under the Goods and Services Tax Act 2003. For the AI Avatar Video Generation SaaS, digital export qualifies where (i) the recipient is not a resident of Samoa; (ii) the service is supplied for use entirely outside Samoa; and (iii) the supplier is registered for VAGST. Input tax credits attributable to such zero-rated exports are refundable under the ordinary VAGST refund mechanism. Where the entity operates as an exempt International Company, zero-rating is irrelevant because no VAGST applies in the first instance; voluntary registration is only necessary if the IC engages in Samoan domestic taxable activity.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Samoa Customs Export Declaration (SED) or Post-Shipment Export Entry
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill evidencing physical export (goods transactions)
Commercial Invoice and executed SaaS / Virtual Avatar Licensing Agreement
Inward Remittance Certificate or Foreign Exchange Proceeds Certificate from a licensed commercial bank in Samoa
Non-Resident Recipient Declaration or official evidence of the customer's foreign establishment
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Under the Tax Administration Act 2012, deliberate or reckless false export zero-rating or refund claims attract a tax shortfall penalty of up to 150%, in addition to late payment surcharges and criminal fines up to WST 100,000 and/or imprisonment up to 7 years for wilful evasion. Unsupported zero-rated claims are retrospectively clawed back with a general 4-year reassessment window and an unlimited window where fraud or wilful misstatement is established. Parallel AML sanctions apply under the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2018 where fabricated export documentation is detected by the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit. Failure to repatriate export proceeds within 180 days triggers penalties and licence conditions under the Exchange Control Act 1976 administered by the Central Bank of Samoa.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Samoa (CBS), Apia, Samoa — statutory administrator of the Exchange Control Act 1976 and operator of the national real-time gross settlement system (Samoa Interbank Payment System, SIPS).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Samoan Tālā (WST) is not an internationally deliverable offshore currency; convertibility exists only through CBS-licensed authorized dealers onshore. Current account transactions (software export receipts, royalties, professional fees) are freely convertible through authorized dealers under delegated CBS authority without prior central bank approval. Capital account transactions (equity injection, foreign loans, share redemption, dividend streaming, liquidation distributions) remain subject to the Exchange Control Act 1976: transactions within a dealer's delegated limit are processed immediately, while transactions above that bandwidth require a CBS capital-account application with a typical 5–10 business day turnaround. Profit remittance for an International Company (IC) is practically feasible but requires (i) proof of genuine distributable profits via examined/audited financials or a registered-agent solvency certificate, (ii) certification that the underlying inward funds entered Samoa through the banking system, and (iii) absence of delinquent Samoan liabilities. For this AI Avatar Video SaaS business, the convertibility profile is low-risk: customers are non-resident, revenue is export service income, and only procurement payments and profit distributions cross the capital account.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Exchange Control Act 1976, all export proceeds — including SaaS and software service receipts — must be repatriated into the Samoan banking system within 90 days from invoice/export date and must be offered for sale to an authorized dealer in exchange for WST unless CBS approves a foreign currency retention limit. Samoa imposes no fixed percentage conversion ratio (e.g., 50% or 80% surrender); the operative rule is effectively full repatriation and offer-and-sale (100%) unless a formal retention approval is granted to fund future foreign-currency procurement. The IC benefits from statutory exchange-control exemptions under the International Companies Act 1987 for dealings exclusively with non-residents, but once SaaS revenue is credited to a Samoan account, the authorized dealer records the inflow as export proceeds and applies the surrender/retention regime.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: USD/foreign-currency operational account (capital escrow optional given zero minimum capital) + WST operating float account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Australia and New Zealand Banking Group (ANZ) — Samoa Branch
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: USD/WST dual-currency operational account; SWIFT MT103 and MT700 clearing capacity

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: LOW as an onshore clearing rail; MEDIUM as an offshore collection adjunct. Samoa has no dedicated Electronic Money Institution licensing class; the Financial Institutions Act 1996 requires a banking license for deposit-taking or domestic payment-system operation, and CBS would not permit an unlicensed offshore EMI (e.g., Wise, Mercury, Airwallex) to hold settlement accounts with CBoS or clearing privileges in SIPS. Offshore EMIs may legally sit upstream of the Samoan banking system: Stripe/Paddle collect client card/ACH receipts abroad, and the EMI issues a SWIFT USD payment to the IC's authorized-dealer account in Samoa. That layered structure is permissible because the EMI has no Samoan nexus, but it does not displace the obligation to bring the SaaS export proceeds into Samoa and report them as export receipts. Stripe and Paddle remain the sanctioned customer-facing rails; neither substitutes for a Samoan authorized-dealer bank account for FX-control and treasury purposes.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No absolute statutory mandate requires directors to appear physically for a 100% non-resident-owned IC. Remote opening is conditionally permitted where the IC appoints a CBS-recognised licensed trust/registered-agent company in Samoa, which performs certified-true-copy verification of passports, proof-of-address, corporate registers, and beneficial-ownership data, and introduces the application to the bank. In practice, BSP and ANZ retain underwriting discretion to require one in-person interview for any ultimate beneficial owner or director before account activation; the decision is driven by jurisdiction risk, source-of-funds clarity, and reputation. For this low-risk AIGC SaaS IC, the realistic path is hybrid onboarding: one executive director or the appointed company secretary attends a single physical interview in Apia, or, where remote-only is preferred, a reputable Samoan licensed registered agent introduces the entity and the bank relies on enhanced video-verification. Apostilled and legalized corporate documents are required; notarization by offshore counsel must be verified by the registered agent.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: International Company shell-structure flags: zero minimum capital, nominee shareholding possibility, tax-exempt-zone status, and offshore-only business scope are commonly screened against FATF shell-company red flags.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified Certificate of Incorporation and Memorandum & Articles of the IC; complete beneficial ownership register showing ultimate natural persons (passport and proof-of-residence); registered-agent compliance opinion issued by a Samoan licensed trust company; current Certificate of Good Standing from the Samoa Financial Services Authority; director/shareholder consent letters; statutory declaration of no nominee ambiguity; 12-month AI SaaS business plan with revenue model, hosting contracts, and client pipeline.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Samoan offshore-center history and prior FATF grey-listing (2019–2024) may trigger enhanced due diligence, correspondent de-risking, or a presumption of low financial-sector transparency.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: CBS and Samoa Financial Services Authority statements confirming FATF delisting in February 2024; summary of the latest Asia/Pacific Group mutual evaluation and the beneficial-ownership register requirements; registered-agent AML/CFT compliance certificate; declaration of non-engagement with sanctioned persons; undertaking to report any shareholding changes within the statutory window; evidence of economic substance via AI licensing agreements and real service contracts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume consumer-facing SaaS receipts involving AI-generated avatar content and digital identity ambiguity may be misread as a money-laundering or terrorist-financing vector.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Stripe/Paddle payout ledgers with customer classification and chargeback history; platform KYB/KYC flow documentation; content-moderation and data-security policies; commercial terms requiring corporate or licensed end-users; bank statements demonstrating clean on-ramp of platform settlements; no crypto or virtual-asset settlement exposure.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: No mandatory upfront equity injection exists because Samoan IC law imposes zero minimum capital; founder funding should be characterized as share capital and remitted via SWIFT MT103 from each shareholder's own account using the originating jurisdiction's capital-account purpose code (e.g., 'S0101 – Capital subscription' or equivalent BOPS guidance code), with the wire narrative 'IC share subscription – [shareholder name] – WS_IC'. The Samoan authorized dealer will verify (i) the IC board resolution allotting shares, (ii) the updated share register reflecting the subscriber, (iii) the registered agent's written acknowledgement, and (iv) absence of local liabilities; the credit is typically available within 1–2 banking days, rising to 5–10 business days where CBS prior approval is triggered by transaction size. All inward capital credits should be escrowed in the USD operational account until compliance release; conversion into WST operating float is limited to lawful domestic administrative expenditure permitted for an IC under the International Companies Act 1987.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: SWIFT MT103 is the principal clearing rail for outbound SaaS disbursements (cloud hosting, GPU subcontracting, licensing fees, contractor payments). For larger procurement of physical IP or infrastructure, a documentary commercial letter of credit under UCP 600 (sight or usance) is available from BSP or ANZ, advised via SWIFT MT700 in USD, although it is atypical for a pure software venture. Domestic WST transfers clear through the CBS-operated Samoa Interbank Payment System (SIPS), while all non-resident payments above the authorized dealer's reporting threshold are captured for CBS balance-of-payments statistics. Dividend, royalty, and other capital-account outflows require: IC board resolution, distribution solvency statement, evidence that the underlying funds entered Samoa through an authorized dealer, and, where the amount exceeds delegated bank power, CBS capital-account assent.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore WST/USD deliverable forward contracts (tenor up to 12 months, rollable) available from BSP and ANZ for commercial hedging of documented export receivables; strictly non-speculative under CBS guidance.
Spot FX transactions through authorized dealers at prevailing interbank rates for immediate operational conversion (T+2 settlement).

Offshore WST/USD non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not legally available in Samoa because the WST has no offshore deliverable market; any offshore NDF would require parental guarantee support and prior CBS consent, and is not recommended for this IC.
Cross-currency swaps (USD/WST) are not offered domestically; synthetic swap structures via layered spot and deposit positions are permissible only where CBS authorization is obtained for each leg.
Interest-rate derivatives (IRS/FRAs) are outside practical scope for this IC; speculative open FX positions are prohibited under CBS regulatory policy.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Samoa International Companies Registry, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days of the annual anniversary of incorporation; fee due on the anniversary date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A late penalty of 50% of the annual fee applies from the first month after the due date; continued non-payment for more than 90 days may trigger administrative strike-off and dissolution of the company.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No mandatory audit is imposed on a Samoa International Company under the International Companies Act 1987; an audit may be required only by voluntary shareholder resolution or where the company undertakes a regulated activity, which does not apply to AI avatar video generation software.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS or Samoa Equivalent to IFRS; where financial statements are voluntarily prepared, they must be maintained at the registered office.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No separate UBO annual confirmation is required under Samoa International Companies law; however, the register of members must be kept up to date and share transfers must be recorded promptly. Beneficial ownership information is required to be maintained internally for AML compliance purposes, but no public UBO register is filed with the authorities.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$500 - US$1,500 per annum if voluntarily audited; otherwise not applicable

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% for an International Company (IC) under the Samoa International Companies Act; general Samoa resident corporate income tax rate is 27%
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Effective rate is nil. ICs are exempt from income tax, capital gains tax, withholding tax on distributions, stamp duty and VAGST on qualifying offshore transactions. The only mandatory payments are the annual international company registration fee and the licensed resident agent fee.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: No Samoa corporate income tax return is required for a Samoa International Company. The statutory compliance filing is the International Company Annual Return filed through the Online Registry of the Samoa Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL). For a hypothetical taxable resident Samoa company, the relevant form is the IRD Annual Income Tax Return filed via the Samoa Inland Revenue Department's e-filing portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The International Company Annual Return is due within 30 days after the anniversary of incorporation. A domestic Samoa taxpayer's income tax return is generally due within three months after year-end; a calendar-year company would file by 31 March.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the exact International Company legal name, IC registration number, Samoa registered office address, and registered agent name.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the IC's own corporate identity. Do not insert beneficial owner TINs or non-resident tax identifiers in this field.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: List current directors, shareholders, share classes, issued shares, and any required ultimate beneficial owner details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide non-resident beneficial owner name, address, passport copy and proof-of-address directly to the licensed Samoa registered agent; this is not an IRD tax declaration.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Confirm the IC maintains a registered office and a licensed registered agent in Samoa, and that the annual government fee has been or will be paid.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Samoa resident agent must sign this declaration; a non-resident director may authenticate by digital signature arranged through the agent.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: State whether the IC relies on the International Companies Act tax exemption and confirm that it has not carried on domestic trade or business with Samoa residents.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not claim the exemption if the IC has a Samoa office, Samoa employees, Samoa-resident board meetings, or local commercial activity; doing so creates a false certification.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Certify under oath or equivalent warning that the return is true, correct and complete, and execute as director or registered agent.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Electronic signatures of non-resident directors are accepted only when authenticated by the Samoa licensed agent.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late IC Annual Return triggers Registrar late-arrears penalties and, after continued default, compulsory strike-off and dissolution. Late filing of a domestic Samoa tax return may result in an IRD late-filing penalty, default assessment, monthly late-payment penalty, prosecution, and travel restriction for directors of the defaulting taxpayer.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% on distributions paid by a Samoa International Company to non-resident shareholders. Samoa's general non-resident dividend withholding tax rate for taxable resident companies is 15%, but the IC is outside the income tax net.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Samoa has a narrow double-taxation agreement network and relies on tax information exchange agreements. Where DTA relief is claimed, the payee must: (i) obtain a Samoa tax residency certificate from the Commissioner of Inland Revenue; (ii) provide a beneficial ownership declaration and, where US-source payments are involved, IRS Form W-8BEN-E; (iii) submit the documents to the withholding agent before payment. A zero-tax IC without actual management and substance is generally denied treaty benefits by source jurisdictions.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Samoa statutory withholding rate on royalties and interest paid by a resident taxpayer to a non-resident is 15%. Because an IC is tax-exempt, royalties and interest paid out by the IC incur no Samoan WHT. Inbound payments to the IC for AI avatar software may be subject to source-country withholding tax, and a Samoa IC will need to demonstrate real economic substance to access any applicable treaty reduction.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No formal Samoa transfer-pricing documentation threshold applies to International Companies. Samoa's tax law contains general anti-avoidance powers to recharacterise non-arm's length transactions. A prudent internal threshold is WST 500,000 in aggregate annual controlled transactions; above this level the IC should maintain simplified Local File and Master File documentation even though Samoan income tax is not levied.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Samoa has not enacted BVI/Cayman-style Economic Substance Regulations, but the International Companies Act requires a Samoa registered office and licensed resident agent. Foreign tax authorities will still apply CFC, managed-and-controlled, place-of-effective-management, and substance-over-form rules to the AI Avatar Video SaaS business. Samoa anti-avoidance law can also disregard an IC facade if the entity engages in actual Samoa-sourced business.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / Sham Tax Exemption Claim
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the AI avatar SaaS platform as a zero-tax Samoa IC while board decisions, software development, sales, customer support, or strategic management are actually performed in a high-tax jurisdiction; filing the annual exemption declaration while carrying on business with Samoa residents; backdating intellectual property assignments to avoid exit tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Commissioner may disregard the IC under Samoa's general anti-avoidance provisions, issue a default assessment on true economic profit, impose a shortfall penalty of up to 150% of the tax evaded, add late-payment interest, and pursue criminal prosecution.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly sign false exemption declarations or orchestrate evasion are jointly and severally liable for civil restitution and fraud penalties. The corporate veil may be pierced when the IC is a mere instrumentality; directors may face travel bans, extradition, disqualification, and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Commercial Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining an IC with no real substance: no board, no staff, no bank account in the IC's name, no physical place of business, no IP control, and no managed and controlled function; routing Stripe and Paddle merchant payouts directly to a foreign controlling entity or individual.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Samoa Registrar may reject the annual return, impose Registry arrears and, after continued non-compliance, strike the IC off and dissolve it. Source-country tax authorities may reclassify the AI software business as resident elsewhere, impose CFC taxation, or disregard the Samoa IC entirely.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Nominee and de facto directors can be disqualified from acting as directors. Where limited liability is used to evade contractual or regulatory debts, directors may be personally exposed to civil claims and restoration costs, and travel bans may be imposed in cross-border tax collection.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting Stripe and Paddle SaaS payments without adequate KYC/CDD on non-resident beneficial owners, failing to monitor suspicious payment patterns, allowing layering through virtual-asset transfers, using the IC structure to obscure sanctioned persons or proceeds of crime, or failing to maintain a beneficial ownership register with the licensed agent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Samoa's Money Laundering Prevention Act and Financial Intelligence Unit regulations authorise civil penalties, confiscation of proceeds, revocation of the registered agent's license, interruption of banking and merchant-account relationships, and criminal prosecution of the IC and its officers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers with knowledge or suspicion of unlawful fund flows can be personally charged with money laundering or financing of terrorism. Penalties include imprisonment up to 14 years, asset forfeiture, fines, travel bans, and permanent disqualification from managing regulated entities.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: False Filing / Fraudulent Misrepresentation in Corporate Registry
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Submitting a materially false annual return to the Samoa International Companies Registry: undisclosed beneficial owners, false confirmation of registered office, forged non-resident director signatures, false no-domestic-business certifications, or concealment of the actual controller of the AI avatar video generation business.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Samoa's International Companies Act and general companies legislation, false statements are punishable by fines and imprisonment; the entity may be struck off, and third parties may recover damages based on the false registry information.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Signing officers are personally liable for false declaration offences. Courts may impose civil restitution beyond corporate assets, order travel bans, disqualify the individual from serving as a director of any Samoa company, and impose custodial sentences.
